newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Mappin seeks stake in Mesbla -source.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Mappin seeks stake in Mesbla -source.

text.p: Brazilian department store chain Mappin, owned by businessman Ricardo Mansur, has proposed buying a controlling stake in ailing retailer Mesbla, a source close to the negotiations said.

The proposal was made earlier this week, said the source, who requested anonymity. He added that local investment bank Banco Pactual, which has been running Mesbla, was also awaiting offers from two U.S. retail chains also interested in Mesbla.
A spokesman for Mansur would not comment on the proposal.
Jose Paulo Amaral, an executive at Pactual, is in the United States to meet with investors and is expected to return to Brazil Monday, a Mesbla spokeswoman said.
Gazeta Mercantil newspaper reported Friday that Mappin has offered $500 million to acquire control of Mesbla.

Once a leading local retailer, Mesbla filed for debt relief under a section of the bankruptcy law equivalent to Chapter 11 reorganization in the U.S. in August 1995. Its debt reportedly now amounts to 900 million reais.
Banco Pactual took over management of Mesbla late last year as part of a plan to restructure the firm's debt.
Since Pactual began to administer Mesbla and seek a solution for the company, the market has speculated about potential buyers for the retailer.
Mansur acquired control of Casa Anglo, the holding company for Mappin department store, in August 1996 and has been seen as the most likely candidate to assume control of Mesbla.
Mansur also owns Brazilian dairy firms Vigor, Leco and Flor da Nata and bank Banco Crefisul.
